label: Headphones & earphones
note: This category passes or fails per product, not per category. A branded pair with published driver size, codec support and battery figures has a real fact sheet. The sub-₹2,000 commodity flood does not — its 'specs' are marketing claims. The required fields below do that filtering automatically, without anyone curating a brand list.

driver_mm.label: Driver size
driver_mm.note: The diameter of the speaker inside each earpiece. A larger driver can move more air, which usually helps bass, but tuning and housing design affect the sound at least as much as size does.

driver_type.label: Driver type
driver_type.note: The technology that makes the sound. Dynamic drivers are the common single-driver design with strong bass; balanced armature units are smaller and more precise in the mids and treble; hybrids combine both to cover each range.

anc.label: Noise cancellation
anc.note: How the model handles outside noise. Passive isolation is just the physical seal; active cancellation uses microphones to counter low steady sound like engines and fans, and works far better on that than on speech.

values_note.Passive only: Blocks sound by physical seal alone, with no electronics.
values_note.ANC: Active cancellation using microphones, typically outward-facing only.
values_note.Hybrid ANC: Microphones both outside and inside the ear, cancelling a wider range more accurately.
values_note.Adaptive ANC: Hybrid cancellation that adjusts continuously to the surrounding noise and the fit in your ear.

enc_calls.label: Call noise reduction
enc_calls.note: Whether extra microphones reduce background noise for the person on the other end of a call. This is separate from noise cancellation, which only affects what you hear.

codecs.label: Bluetooth codecs
codecs.note: How audio is compressed over Bluetooth. Both the phone and the headphone must support a codec for it to be used; otherwise both fall back to SBC, the basic one. iPhones use AAC and never LDAC.

bluetooth.label: Bluetooth
bluetooth.note: The Bluetooth version. Later versions improve range and power use, but the phone has to support the same version for the benefit to apply.

multipoint.label: Multipoint pairing
multipoint.note: Whether the model can hold connections to two devices at once, so a call on the phone interrupts music from the laptop without re-pairing.

battery_hr.label: Battery life
battery_hr.note: Playback time on one charge, as quoted by the maker. Makers usually measure with noise cancellation off and at moderate volume, so real figures run lower.

battery_buds_hr.label: Battery, earbuds
battery_buds_hr.note: Playback time from the earbuds alone before returning them to the case. This is the figure that decides whether they last a long flight or a full workday.

battery_case_hr.label: Battery, with case
battery_case_hr.note: Total listening time including recharges from the case. It is the headline number makers advertise, but the earbuds' own runtime is what limits a single session.

fast_charge.label: Fast charge
fast_charge.note: How much playback a short top-up gives, such as 10 minutes for 2 hours. It is the figure that matters when you have forgotten to charge before leaving.

ip_rating.label: Water and dust resistance
ip_rating.note: Sealing against dust and water. IPX4 handles sweat and light rain, which is the practical bar for exercise; IP67 and above survive brief immersion. Cases are often rated separately from the earbuds.

connector.label: Connector
connector.note: The plug fitted to a wired model. A phone without a headphone socket needs a USB-C or Lightning model, or an adapter.

impedance_ohm.label: Impedance
impedance_ohm.note: Electrical resistance in ohms. Above roughly 100 ohms, a phone or laptop may not drive the headphone loudly enough without a separate amplifier; low-impedance models run fine from anything.

frequency_response.label: Frequency response
frequency_response.note: The range of pitches the earphone reproduces, such as 20 Hz - 20 kHz. Nearly every model quotes roughly the range of human hearing, so it rarely distinguishes two products and says nothing about tuning.

mic.label: Microphone
mic.note: Whether the model has a microphone for calls and voice assistants.

wired_fallback.label: Wired listening
wired_fallback.note: Whether the model can be used with a cable when the battery is flat or when Bluetooth is not allowed, such as on some aircraft entertainment systems.

launch_month.label: Announced
launch_month.note: The month the maker announced this model, as YYYY-MM. Audio models are often refreshed quietly, and this separates a current unit from last year's stock.

model_number.label: Model number
model_number.note: The maker's own model code. Regional variants of the same marketing name can differ in codec support, so the model number is the reliable identifier.

form_factor.label: Form factor
form_factor.note: The physical style, which decides fit, isolation and battery. Over-ear cups block more noise passively than in-ear tips; open-ear designs deliberately let outside sound through.

sensitivity_db.label: Sensitivity
sensitivity_db.note: How loud the headphone plays for a given amount of power. Higher sensitivity means more volume from the same source, which matters when pairing with a phone rather than an amplifier.

spatial_audio.label: Spatial audio
spatial_audio.note: Whether the model can place sound in a simulated 3D space, sometimes tracking head movement. It usually needs the maker's own phone or app to work.

hi_res_certified.label: Hi-Res Audio certified
hi_res_certified.note: Whether the Japan Audio Society has certified the model for high-resolution playback. Over Bluetooth this requires a matching codec such as LDAC, and the certification covers capability rather than tuning quality.

anc_depth_db.label: Stated noise reduction
anc_depth_db.note: How much noise the maker claims the cancellation removes, in decibels. Every maker measures this differently, so treat it as the maker's own claim rather than a figure comparable across brands.

transparency_mode.label: Transparency mode
transparency_mode.note: Whether the model can pipe outside sound in deliberately, so you can hear traffic or an announcement without removing the earphones.

charging_case_wireless.label: Wireless charging case
charging_case_wireless.note: Whether the case can charge on a wireless pad rather than only by cable.

bluetooth_range_m.label: Stated range
bluetooth_range_m.note: The wireless range the maker quotes, measured with nothing in the way. Walls and bodies cut it substantially in practice.

controls.label: Controls
controls.note: How you change track or volume. Physical buttons are harder to trigger by accident than touch panels, which can respond to rain or to adjusting the fit.

app_support.label: Companion app
app_support.note: Whether a maker's app exists to change the tuning, remap controls or update the firmware. Without one, the model is fixed as it shipped.

eq_customisable.label: Adjustable EQ
eq_customisable.note: Whether the sound balance can be changed, usually through the companion app. Some models offer only fixed presets rather than full control.

wear_detection.label: Wear detection
wear_detection.note: Whether the model pauses automatically when removed from the ear and resumes when put back.

voice_assistant.label: Voice assistants
voice_assistant.note: Which assistants can be summoned directly. Most models pass through whatever the connected phone uses, so this matters mainly for wake-word support.

foldable.label: Folds for storage
foldable.note: Whether the headband or cups fold to pack smaller. It decides whether the model fits in a bag rather than needing a dedicated case.

ear_tip_sizes.label: Ear tip sizes included
ear_tip_sizes.note: Which tip sizes come in the box. Fit determines both seal and how well noise cancellation works, so the range of included sizes matters more than it appears.

colours.label: Colours
colours.note: The finishes this model is sold in.

spec_url.label: Official spec sheet
spec_url.note: A link to the maker's own specification page for this exact model. It is the source a disputed fact here should be checked against, and it outranks any marketplace listing.

spec_checked_version.label: Spec sheet version
spec_checked_version.note: Which revision of the maker's spec page these facts were read from, as a date or version. Makers quietly edit spec pages after launch, so this records which wording was in front of us.

sanity.note: Never record a claim that cannot be checked against a published spec. 'Deep bass', 'studio sound' and 'crystal clear calls' are not facts and have no field here.
sanity.battery: Battery figures are the maker's claim at their own volume and codec. Record as stated; do not present as measured.
